title: A Poison Like No Other: How Microplastics Corrupted Our Planet and Our Bodies
author: Matt Simon
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. Explanatory environmental science reporting, not a toxicology training manual or personal health protocol. Ecology and pollution dominate, T11=-10; policy proposals are subsidiary, T12=0. The described exposure evidence should not be treated as proof of every proposed clinical consequence. No serious veto established. Expert review is favorable but reader reception is mixed; not selected for the 200 praised-book group.
notes: Scientific reporting and extensive notes support exposure claims; human health implications remain less settled.
Connects production, material degradation and transport through several environmental systems.
Useful life-cycle and upstream-versus-downstream intervention lessons, with limited broader strategic coverage.
Explains fragmentation, dispersal and persistence; causal health estimates require caution.
D=8, moderate confidence from Norris's Oryx review, Kirkus and readers. Sea, soil and air cases introduce distinct pathways; the solutions section is short. No direct whole-book audit.
Material persistence and waste-system constraints are durable; specific toxicological knowledge will develop.
Materials and production partly fit, but environmental effects dominate.
Experienced science journalist with favorable specialist review; no claim of toxicological consensus on all outcomes.
A clear route through different environmental compartments makes the account accessible.
Readable explanation with emotive language that can exceed the measured tone of the evidence.

title: The World the Plague Made: The Black Death and the Rise of Europe
author: James Belich
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. Explanatory global economic history, not medical advice or specialist training. Disease is the initiating and recurring central factor, T11=-10; trade, technology and economic transformation organize the account, so T12=0 despite imperial applications. Central period roughly 1350-1800, endpoint 1800. Cowen challenges the evidence for sustained living-standard gains and the simple per-capita wealth inference. Stoll and Mazo praise the historical synthesis, while Belich explicitly treats plague as one important cause rather than the sole explanation. The inspected criticism creates substantial uncertainty but does not establish V9 with high confidence after these defenses. Reader response is mixed; not selected for the praised-book quota.
notes: Extensive historical evidence supports many cases; the long causal chain from mortality to later divergence is less secure.
Integrates demography, labor scarcity, technology adoption, trade, institutions and imperial expansion.
Scarcity-driven substitution and demand changes offer transferable questions, not a universal law of collapse or growth.
Develops several mechanisms while the relative contribution of plague remains difficult to isolate.

D=8, moderate confidence from Mazo, the Inquisitive Biologist and contrasting readers. Regional cases add substantial historical learning; some downstream connections require the reader to reconstruct the argument. Length alone is not a penalty.
The evidence and comparative questions should remain useful despite disagreement about the synthesis.
Trade, technological substitution, production and global scaling fit strongly.
Established historian with serious specialist attention; praise is not unanimity about the main thesis.
Thematic organization helps, but the extensive comparative history can overwhelm a general reader.
Careful qualifications coexist with memorable but overly simple formulations.

title: This Is Vegan Propaganda: And Other Lies the Meat Industry Tells You
author: Ed Winters
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. The author explicitly frames veganism as an ethical stance, not specifically a diet. Contents show moral argument, agriculture, environmental effects, health and social barriers; two health chapters do not make the whole book a health-advice work under V7. One communication chapter does not establish H7. No evidence of extremist advocacy was found; manifesto language, activism and proposed reform alone do not establish V5 or V6. The sample is strongly argumentative, but a serious epistemic or allegiance-based veto was not established from the inspected evidence. Environmental and health themes receive T11=-10, and moral philosophy is central, T12=-10. Strong reader praise does not establish expert consensus; not selected for the quota.
notes: Many citations and interviews support descriptive claims; empirical evidence and moral premises need to be distinguished, with limited opposing specialist evidence inspected.
Links animal production, consumer behavior, regulation and environmental effects, mainly toward a single normative conclusion.
Some reasoning about externalities and concealed production costs transfers; direct domain utility is limited.
Describes supply-chain practices and social incentives, but broad dietary and social outcomes require more causal support.

D=6, moderate confidence from the publisher sample, contents and contrasting reading reports. Farming practices and institutional cases add information; graphic examples and persuasion can repeat the core conclusion.
Ethical questions persist; particular health and environmental estimates need updating.
Food production is relevant only peripherally to this collection's central technical interests.
Experienced advocate; substantial independent specialist validation of the entire synthesis was not established.
Clear thematic progression, with some readers finding the opening graphic material difficult.
Accessible but categorical and persuasive rather than consistently qualified.

title: The Watchman's Rattle: Thinking Our Way Out of Extinction
author: Rebecca D. Costa
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. General social explanation rather than technical training. Historical cases support a contemporary complexity argument, so no single historical endpoint applies. The claimed cognitive threshold is weakly established in the inspected evidence; the Suite101 review reproduced by the author directly questions its circularity and the proposed insight remedy. That non-specialist criticism does not by itself satisfy V9's substantial specialist-criticism requirement, and limited direct coverage prevents a confident V1 finding. Retained with low confidence and low priority, not selected on praise. Environmental and political applications do not predominate over the claimed general cognitive mechanism, so thematic deductions are zero. Broad social problem-solving is not automatically personal life support under V7.
notes: The proposed biological limit is inferred from selected cases; direct validation of the historical causal claim is not established.
Touches several social systems but connections depend heavily on the same untested framework.
Looking beyond symptoms and using multiple approaches are reusable but familiar ideas.
The cognitive-threshold explanation risks restating failure rather than identifying an independently testable cause.

D=5, moderate confidence from the author-reproduced critical review and contrasting reader reports. The recurring collapse sequence adds limited learning; discussion of different cultural obstacles is more useful.
Complexity management persists, but current-event framing and claims of a novel solution reduce durability.
Systems thinking and technological change fit partly; industrial mechanisms are thin.
Business experience and prominent endorsements do not establish specialist validation of the central theory.
Accessible anecdotes and repeated structure aid reading but weaken cumulative development.
Promotional and categorical language reduces precision.
